lines.text: Near the top of Taipei 101 hangs a giant golden ball. Its only job is to fight the wind.
Tall towers bend in strong wind, and rock back and forth at their own natural rhythm.
This ball weighs six hundred sixty tonnes, is welded from forty one steel plates, and hangs like a pendulum.
It's tuned to swing at the same rhythm as the building.
So when the tower leans one way, the heavy ball lags behind and pulls it back.
Dampers around the ball soak up the motion as heat, cutting the sway by up to forty percent.
In 2015, Typhoon Soudelor pushed it a full meter, its biggest swing ever recorded.
